rationale: This is essentially a conjunction of two well-documented anomalies (high capex/assets = investment effect, low operating cash flow = cash-based profitability effect) with no genuinely new interaction mechanism, and it closely revisits the archive's already-tested capex×oancf combination in level rather than change form.

The tangibility×earnings-instability conjunction is a coherent operating-rigidity story that is not a direct restatement of the investment or profitability anomalies, though a 3-period VOL on annual earnings is noisy and the PPE/at leg risks capturing stale industry composition even after IND_ZSCORE.

Internally consistent and distinct from the archive's change-based inventory/liquidity signal, but the oancf/lct leg is close to a standard distress/cash-flow-coverage measure and may drive most of the spread, so the incremental role of inventory composition needs to be verified.

The second leg is internally inconsistent with the expected sign — falling working capital is a low-accrual signal that the accrual anomaly associates with *higher* future returns — so the two MIN legs pull in opposite directions and the composite's natural sign is ambiguous.

Directionally consistent and the prior-weakness conditioning is a sensible way to separate turnaround from demand collapse, but the triple MIN makes the score a min-of-mins that will be dominated by whichever leg is most extreme, likely producing thin, unstable extreme portfolios; also note the inventory-decline leg alone is the published inventory-growth anomaly.

The lead leg is simply the inverse asset-growth anomaly, and the Δ(ceq/at) "repair" leg conflates retained-earnings recovery with equity issuance, which the net-issuance anomaly links to *lower* returns, so the composite mixes a rediscovery with a sign-ambiguous component under the same triple-MIN template as the preceding proposal.
